source: Zhang, Xu, Liu et al., "Software Architecture Recovery with Information Fusion", ESEC/FSE 2023 (DOI 10.1145/3611643.3616285) — the 'Labeled' (industry-collaborator-labeled) ground-truth tier of the SARIF replication package.
retrieved_via: raw.githubusercontent.com, converted verbatim to RSF (group name -> `contain <group> <file>`; entity paths kept as published, repo-relative)
format: RSF `contain <cluster> <file>` tuples converted 1:1 from the published JSON (structure[].name -> cluster, structure[].nested[].name -> file); entities are repo-relative paths (root basenames + include/libxml/, python/, macos/)
license_note: The SARIF replication repository is anonymous and carries NO LICENSE file (all-rights-reserved by default), so the converted reference.rsf and the retrieved JSON are LOCAL-ONLY (see .gitignore), mirroring the nopCommerce precedent (P§19.6). Reproduce with: python -c "import json,pathlib; gt=json.loads(pathlib.Path('references/libxml2/libxml2-2.4.22-GT.json').read_text(encoding='utf-8')); pathlib.Path('references/libxml2/reference.rsf').write_bytes(('\n'.join(sorted(f'contain {g[\"name\"]} {i[\"name\"]}' for g in gt['structure'] for i in g.get('nested',[])))+'\n').encode())" after downloading the dataset_url.
notes: Third usable public C/C++ ground truth (after ITK and bash). ARCHITECTURAL SHAPE CONTRAST: unlike bash (whose GT clusters coincide with its static-library build targets), the libxml2 GT's 18 clusters are semantic module groups INSIDE the single libxml2 shared-library target — the monolithic-library case where the build graph deliberately cannot carry the decomposition. Expected/observed: the no-curation floor and target-based pipeline collapse here (the C-language analogue of the C# regime), which bounds the deterministic-first thesis by build-graph shape rather than by language.
